root_idea.summary: A conventional placeholder used in place of an unnamed or unspecified individual, especially a person; related usage extends the designation to a particular nonhuman animal.
root_idea.development: The root's lexical orientation is substitution by a nonspecific name: فلان serves as a kināyah for a person, while related definite and relational forms support animal designation and reference by association.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized masculine singular citation form فلان rather than the Quranic accusative surface form فلانًا.

senses.definition: An unnamed or unspecified human person; “such a one.”
senses.usage_conditions: A substitute for a person's proper name, including reference to either a male or a female. In the Quranic occurrence it appears in the accusative construction فُلَانًا خَلِيلًا, referring to the person taken as an intimate friend.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular nonhuman animal designated without naming it, such as a particular camel or other beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded with the definite article, in constructions such as riding or milking the particular animal. This is distinct from the Quranic human-placeholder use of فُلَانٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relational adjective derived from فُلَان, referring to someone in relation to an unnamed “such a one.”
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The suffix ي renders the form indeterminate; adding the definite article makes it determinate, as in a person identified in relation to such a one.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Human placeholder and definite nonhuman-animal branches are represented; inflectional and vocative details are not separate meanings.
